results.title: ML best practices in PyTorch dev conf 2018 – DVC
results.content: Learn from AI, ML & data leaders. In the Machine Learning (ML) field tools and techniques for best practices are just starting to be developed. At the PyTorch developer conference (PTDC-18), several speakers including \*\*Jerome Pesenti, VP of AI from Facebook\*\* and \*\*Andrej Karpathy, Director of Tesla AI\*\* spoke about best practices for machine learning development. The issues discussed included applying traditional software development techniques like unit testing, CI/CD systems, automated deployment, version control, and more to the ML field. In this blog post, we will go over the best practices ideas from PTDC-18 and the future of ML tool developments. In the PTDC-18 keynote speech, **Jerome Pesenti** described the motivation and goals of PyTorch project and what the future of machine learning looks like. Traditional software engineering has many useful tools and techniques which can either be repurposed for Machine Learning development or used as a source for ideas in developing new tools. Engineering practices for software 2.0. Software 2.0 best practices.

results.title: DVC For Real Projects: Smarter Dataset Versioning
results.content: # DVC for Real Projects: Smarter Dataset Versioning. Why Traditional Dataset Management Falls Short Static storage is a recipe […]. Version Datasets Easily with DVC. ### Static storage is a recipe for confusion. Without proper versioning, it’s easy to lose track of what’s changed. But large files and datasets? One small change to a dataset might throw off your entire model pipeline if it’s not well-tracked. ## Enter DVC: The Git for Your Data. **Data Version Control (DVC)** works alongside Git but specializes in handling large data files and machine learning pipelines. It tracks changes in your datasets, just like Git tracks changes in your code. ### Data storage is decoupled, but metadata stays in Git. Your actual data lives in remote storage (S3, GCP, SSH, etc.), while lightweight metadata files go into Git. That means faster commits and zero bloating of your codebase. ### Keep large files out of Git. Once DVC is tracking your files, Git just handles the `.dvc` metadata.
